ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. The skill requires this before every fix round, and it sets the re-review rules.
ACTION: Edit `docs/sync.md` line 12. Change `--dry_run` to `--dry-run`.
ACTION: Commit that one edit with the message "docs: fix --dry-run flag name in sync.md".
ACTION: Append a note to the implementer's report file in `.sdd/14-buoy-sync/`. The note says I fixed F1 myself, that it is one word in `docs/sync.md:12`, that it changes no behavior, and that no test covers it.
ACTION: Run `scripts/review-package specs/plans/14-buoy-sync.md <BASE> <HEAD>` with the BASE and HEAD that fix-loop.md and file-handoffs.md give for a re-review. Keep only the path it reports.
ACTION: Dispatch a scoped re-review with `re-review-prompt.md`, model `sonnet`. The prompt gives the verbatim F1 text, the new diff file path, and the Global Constraints block copied from the plan. It asks for an ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED verdict on F1 and a check for new Critical or Important issues. It does not tell the reviewer what to ignore.

If fix-loop.md says something that conflicts with this order, I follow fix-loop.md and send the fix to a fix subagent instead.

Task 3 review found one Important issue. `docs/sync.md:12` names the flag `--dry_run`, but the code, the help text and the tests use `--dry-run`. I am fixing the doc myself and sending it to a scoped re-review. I will not mark Task 3 complete until that re-review comes back clean.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The skill lets me fix a wrong name in docs myself because the change is confined to one file and alters no behavior. Nothing in the code or tests reads `docs/sync.md`, so the edit cannot break anything.
- The re-review still runs, because a reviewer must confirm the fix. The controller cannot approve its own change.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
